title: Decouple path semantics from runtime platform; use target-platform paths
context: Cross-platform spawn resolver was tested with Linux CI's POSIX path semantics, breaking Windows path assertions. Tests mock Windows execution but ran on Linux hosts, causing path.join() to produce incorrect separators. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.).
decision: Switch to explicit path.win32/path.posix selection based on target platform variable, not runtime platform. Resolves paths using correct semantics regardless of host OS.
consequences: Windows path resolution verified correctly on Linux CI without platform-gated test skips
Enables accurate multi-platform testing on single-platform CI runners
Path behavior now explicitly tied to intended target, not accidental host platform
Test assertion now uses win32.join() to match production path semantics
alternatives_rejected: Conditional test skip for non-Windows hosts (reduces CI coverage, hides bugs)
Mock the path module (adds complexity, fragments test maintainability)
Only test on Windows runner (defeats purpose of multi-platform testing)
